renders._yaml:
- component: card
  id: flagged_ranges
  title: Ranges flagged as foreign
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of ranges FCS-GX flags as foreign, with the number of distinct sequences they sit on, and the bar splits them by the action it recommends. It answers how much of the assembly needs cleaning and how.
    How to read: EXCLUDE drops a whole sequence, TRIM cuts a range at a sequence end and FIX masks a range inside a sequence. A clean assembly shows zero here, and the table still lists it as screened.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/ncbi/fcs/FCS-GX-quickstart.md
  column: seq_id
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: action
  filter_expr: col('action') != 'none'
  caption: ranges, by recommended action
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: flagged_bases
  title: Bases flagged as foreign
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total count of bases in flagged ranges, with the median and the largest range beside it, and the bars rank the taxonomic division groups of the contaminants by bases. It answers how much sequence is foreign and which kind of organism it comes from.
    How to read: a division group that dominates, bacteria for instance, points to the likely source of the contamination. Compare with the number of ranges to tell a few long contaminants from many short ones.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ncbi/fcs/main/README.md
  column: flagged_bp
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: division_group
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: bases, by division group

- component: figure
  title: Foreign bases per assembly
  description: |-
    Each bar is the count of bases FCS-GX flags as foreign in one assembly, stacked by the taxonomic division of the contaminant. It answers which assemblies are contaminated and by what.
    How to read: an assembly with no bar is clean. A tall bar of one colour is a single contaminant source, and several colours point to mixed contamination, so open the table to inspect the ranges before trimming.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: genome
    y: flagged_bp
    color: division
    labels:
      genome: Assembly
      flagged_bp: Bases flagged as foreign
      division: Taxonomic division

- component: table
  title: Contamination calls
  description: |-
    Each row is a range FCS-GX flags as foreign, with the action it recommends, its taxonomic division, the top taxon of the contaminant, the share of the range the contaminant covers and its length. An assembly with nothing flagged keeps one row with action none. It answers exactly which sequences to exclude, trim or fix.
    How to read: filter by action to plan the cleaning, and read the top taxon to confirm the contaminant is plausible for this assembly.
